newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African JSE to change all tick sizes to one cent.
newsitem.headline: S.African JSE to change all tick sizes to one cent.

text.p: South Africa's Johannesburg Stock Exchange said on Monday that it is to implement a standard tick size of one cent across all its shares in order to help boost liquidity.
"International research shows that smaller spreads improve the liquidity of the market in both low priced and less liquid stocks," the JSE said in a statement.

A tick measures the movement of a stock price and currently varies according to the value of the share. For instant a share valued over 5,000 cents moves in ticks of 25 cents up or down, while a stock between 501-1,000 cents moves in ticks of two cents.
From November 25 all shares will move in ticks of one cent irrespective of the value of the share.
"A one cent tick size optimises free market forces in price formation," the JSE said.
The current system creates problems as dealers may be reluctant to trade in stocks that have prices near the boundaries between different tick sizes.
Tick size can also influence the price at which a company lists it shares and will make the conversion of foreign currency prices easier.
